== Biography ==

The Dodo is a solemn creature of Wonderland who arrives on shore among the animals that fell into the pool. Rising to its feet with particular formality, the Dodo assumes the manner of one accustomed to command, proposing that the meeting adjourn in favor of "more energetic remedies" to address the company's dampness. When the Eaglet interrupts with a demand to "speak English," the Dodo responds in an offended tone—wounded by the suggestion that its language is unclear—yet persists in its purposes undeterred.

It is the Dodo who proposes the Caucus-race as a solution to their predicament, and when asked to explain what such a thing might be, the Dodo insists that "the best way to explain it is to do it." With methodical authority, the Dodo then marks out a race-course in a circle, noting with offhand precision that "the exact shape doesn't matter," before positioning all the party members along the course. Through these actions, the Dodo reveals itself as the architect of ceremony in Wonderland—dignified, somewhat pompous in its speech, yet practical and determined in its execution of the most peculiar of plans.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. Dodo seems to regard Alice as part of the assembled party on the shore, acknowledging her presence among the creatures.

'''[[Eaglet]]''' — friendly_rivalry. The Eaglet's challenge to Dodo's elaborate manner of speech appears to spark spirited exchange, though the two creatures continue to interact without apparent lasting discord during the Caucus-race.
